issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the one-dimensional estimate claims, for all s > 1/2, the embedding H^s(I) ↪ C^{0,s−1/2}(Ī). For s ≥ 3/2 the Hölder exponent s−1/2 ≥ 1, and |v(x)−v(y)| ≤ C|x−y|^α with α ≥ 1 forces v to be constant, so the embedding is false for the nonconstant functions of H^s(I); it is also not the standard (non-endpoint) embedding. The theorem applications take s = max(p−1, ε), so p ≥ 3 (s = p−1 ≥ 2) rests on this invalid step. The lemma's statement is nevertheless true — the one-sided vanishing v = 0 on (−δ,0) yields |v(x)| ≲ x^{s−1/2}‖v‖_{H^s} by an iterated fundamental-theorem/Cauchy–Schwarz argument (using v(0)=v'(0)=…=0), and the s ≤ 1/2 case follows by interpolation — but the proof as written does not establish it.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses of the three theorems consist only of the boundary-distance bounds (eq:boundary-errors)–(eq:boundary-errors-small), δ ≤ δ₀, δ ≲ h, and solution regularity; they do not control the mismatch region. The energy proof asserts Ω_δ∖Ω ⊂ U_δ(∂Ω) without proof, and all three proofs invoke lem:strip, whose hypotheses (Ω ⊂ Ω_δ and the strip inclusion eq:strip-assumption) are not among the theorems' assumptions. These inclusions do not follow from the stated hypotheses: for a smooth annulus Ω one can construct a smooth Ω_δ with ∂Ω_δ ⊂ U_δ(∂Ω), ∂Ω ⊂ U_δ(∂Ω_δ) and ‖q−id‖_{L∞(∂Ω_δ)} ≤ δ that fills the hole; then Ω_δ∖Ω contains a fixed-size region on which Δu^e + f_δ = O(1), so the consistency error does not vanish and ‖u^e−u_h‖ stays O(1) as h → 0, contradicting all three estimates (they are false as stated). Moreover, the hypothesis Ω ⊂ Ω_δ of lem:strip fails for the two-sided oscillatory perturbations used in the paper's own numerical studies, so the lemma cannot be invoked as stated even in the intended setting (its proof never actually uses Ω ⊂ Ω_δ).

issues.failure_explanation: The theorems assume only that each ∂Ω_δ is smooth, with bounds on δ and (unboundedly above) δ_n, and no uniformity in the family. The proofs however need: (i) lem:strip's normal-coordinate hypothesis, i.e. reach(∂Ω_δ) > δ, for the mismatch estimates in all three proofs; (ii) for the H¹ proof, the closest-point map q_δ to be well defined and smooth with bounded derivatives on the fixed-width tube U_{δ₂}(∂Ω_δ) with δ₂ ~ 1 — the paper itself fixes 'δ₂ ~ 1 … to prevent blow-up in higher derivatives', and the constants in the u_*^e construction (eq:cutoff-bound, eq:u-star-hp1-bound, eq:grad-u-star-bound) require this; (iii) for the L² proof, elliptic regularity ‖φ‖_{H²(Ω_δ)} ≲ ‖e_h‖ with a constant uniform in the geometry. Smooth approximate boundaries with amplitude δ, δ_n → 0, but curvature ~ δ_n²/δ → ∞ (reach → 0) satisfy every stated hypothesis yet violate (i)–(iii), so the proofs do not apply to them: the geometry is not quantified by (δ, δ_n) alone.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a uniform geometric-regularity assumption on the family {∂Ω_δ} (e.g., reach(∂Ω_δ) ≥ c₀ > 0, or uniformly bounded C^k-norms of the closest-point maps q_δ on U_{δ₂}(∂Ω_δ)) to the three theorems; the existing proofs and rates then apply verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: All three error estimates are unproven for approximate-boundary families without uniform reach/curvature control: the strip-estimate constants, the H¹ cutoff construction, and the L² dual regularity are not controlled by the stated hypotheses.
issues.title: Uniform geometric regularity of ∂Ω_δ (reach/curvature) is needed by the proofs but never assumed
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard hypothesis addition preserving all conclusions and rates, but it genuinely weakens the advertised claim that the geometry is quantified by boundary-location and normal errors (δ, δ_n) alone, excluding a natural class of fine-scale oscillatory approximate boundaries — a limited weakening with no new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The residual bound ‖Δu^e + f_δ‖_{H^s(U_δ(∂Ω))} ≲ ‖u^e‖_{H^{s+2}(U_δ(∂Ω))} (eq:delta-s, reused in eq:l2-termII-residual) silently drops the data contribution: f_δ extends f = −Δu and (eq:f-delta-ext) controls it only by ‖f‖_{H^s(Ω)} ≲ ‖u‖_{H^{s+2}(Ω)}, a global interior norm with no tube-norm bound. In the energy and H¹ arguments the omitted term δ^{s+1}‖f‖_{H^s(Ω)} ≤ h^{s+1}‖f‖ = h^p‖u‖_{H^{p+1}(Ω)} is absorbed by the h^p-term, so those proofs survive once the term is inserted. In the L² argument the same term enters Term II multiplied by the dual factor (δ^{1/2}h^{3/2}+δ)‖φ‖_{H²}, producing δ^{s+1}‖f‖_{H^s(Ω)} (δ^p‖u‖_{H^{p+1}(Ω)} for p ≥ 2), which is bounded by neither h^{p+1}‖u‖_{H^{p+1}(Ω)} (it is one h-order larger) nor the δ-terms (which carry only tube norms of u^e). For p = 1 the H^ε-bound on f needed even to write the estimate is not implied by u ∈ H²(Ω). Hence the stated L² estimate is not established by the proof; the analysis indicates a data-mismatch term (up to δ^p‖f‖_{H^{p−1}(Ω)}, sharply ~δ^{s+3/2}‖f‖) is missing from eq:l2-error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing contribution to eq:l2-error — e.g., a term δ^{s+1}‖f‖_{H^s(Ω)} (or the sharper δ^{s+3/2}‖f‖_{H^s(Ω)}, via an argument exploiting the dual solution's vanishing across the mismatch layer) — and, for p = 1, hypothesize f ∈ H^ε(Ω); alternatively supply the sharper layer argument showing the term is higher order.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal-order L² error estimate (thm:l2-error) is not established as stated: the right-hand side of eq:l2-error lacks a data-mismatch term and, for p = 1, the needed f-regularity is unhypothesized; the abstract's claim of an L² estimate whose geometry contribution consists only of the stated δ-terms is unreliable. The energy and H¹ theorems are unaffected, since the same omitted term is absorbable there.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the geometric errors satisfy $\delta \sim h^2$ and $\delta_n \sim h$, assuming that $\partial\Omega$ is sufficiently smooth.
For the energy norm, the boundary location error enters with an \(h^{-1/2}\)-amplification, and optimal order convergence of order \(h^p\) requires \(\delta \lesssim h^{p+1/2}\).

For the \(L^2\)-norm, the geometry contribution appears as a separate additive term, and optimal order convergence of order \(h^{p+1}\) requires \(\delta \lesssim h^{p+1}\), while the estimate is also insensitive to the normal approximation error \(\delta_n\).
The numerical experiments confirm the theoretical predictions and illustrate how the different geometric error components influence convergence in practice.

issues.failure_explanation: For p = 2 with δ ~ h², the paper's own theory requires δ ≲ h^{p+1/2} = h^{5/2} for optimal energy convergence and δ ≲ h^{p+1} = h³ for optimal L² convergence; both are violated since h² > h^{5/2} and h² > h³ for h < 1. The theory therefore predicts suboptimal rates — energy ≈ h^{3/2} (from the h^{−1/2}δ term) and L² ≈ h² (from the δ term) — whereas the text reports optimal energy (h²) and L² (h³) convergence and asserts agreement with the analysis. The reported rates thus exceed, rather than agree with, the theoretical predictions; the gap is acknowledged only for the H¹-seminorm. The figure caption ('the energy and L² norms retain optimal convergence … in agreement with the analysis') and the conclusion's blanket statement that the experiments 'confirm the theoretical predictions' inherit the misrepresentation.
